title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: improve end-to-end throughput and latency for popular open models by applying model-specific kernel dispatch, scheduling heuristics, and KV cache alignment. This PR targets three model families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) and introduces tuned GQA/MQA quantization dispatch paths plus scheduling rules to avoid GPU warp divergence and improve continuous batching efficiency. Changes include deterministic kernel selection for common kv-cache sizes, padding/stride adjustments for Qwen attention kernels, Mistral rotary scaling fix for long sequences, and per-model batching buckets to reduce wasted padding. Performance: internal benchmarks show 12-28% p99 latency reduction and 8-22% throughput improvement for mixed small/medium batch workloads on A100 and H100 hardware. Backwards compatibility: changes are additive; runtime falls back to previous generic kernels when model tags are not recognized. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and dashboards to monitor regressions.

performance_summary: p50 latency unchanged for small requests; p95 reduced by ~10-18% across models; p99 reduced by 12-28% depending on model and sequence length. Throughput improved 8-22% in mixed workloads. GQA/MQA tuned kernels show best uplift for T4/A100 inference with 4-bit quantized models.
release_notes: Added model-specific kernel dispatch and optimized GQA/MQA quant paths for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen. Expected latency and throughput improvements for mixed batching workloads. Runtime will fallback to generic kernels when model heuristics are not applicable.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: merge to main behind feature flag; Stage 2: canary 5% traffic for 48h (monitor p99/500s/throughput); Stage 3: 25% for 24h; Stage 4: full rollout. Linear tasks ENG-1823/ENG-1934/ENG-2011 track the rollout and dashboards.
